categories.main_business_segments: TOMOKU operates three main business segments: corrugated cardboard (manufacturing and sales of corrugated sheets, cases, and printed cartons), housing (design, construction, and sales of detached houses, mainly through Sweden House and related subsidiaries), and logistics/warehousing (cargo transport and storage services).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced corrugator technology, including proprietary high-speed machines, and focuses on resource- and energy-efficient packaging designs. In housing, it emphasizes high-insulation, high-sealing construction methods inspired by Swedish standards, and integrates prefabricated components for efficiency and sustainability.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include manufacturers of processed foods, beverages, and consumer goods (notably Ito En, a major beverage company), as well as individual homebuyers in Japan seeking high-quality, energy-efficient homes. The logistics segment serves both internal group needs and external clients, mainly in retail and manufacturing.
categories.geographic_coverage: TOMOKU's primary operations are in Japan, with significant manufacturing and sales presence. It also operates in the United States (Southland Box), Sweden (Tomoku Hus AB), and Vietnam (Tomoku Vietnam), with recent expansion in Southeast Asia through acquisitions.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates mainly midstream and downstream in the supply chain: it processes raw materials into packaging and housing products, delivers finished goods to end-users, and provides logistics and warehousing services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening high-quality, high-productivity manufacturing, expanding overseas, and developing environmentally friendly products. R&D focuses on resource-saving packaging, automation, CO2 reduction, and enhancing housing insulation and sustainability. The group also invests in digitalization, workplace safety, and diversity.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through the sale of manufactured products (corrugated packaging, housing units), construction contracts, and logistics/warehousing services. The company also receives income from related services such as housing renovation and after-sales support.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors in the corrugated packaging segment include Rengo, Oji Holdings, and other large Japanese packaging firms. In housing, TOMOKU competes with other high-end homebuilders. The company positions itself as a quality and innovation leader, especially in eco-friendly packaging and premium housing.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, TOMOKU reported consolidated sales of 219.6 billion yen, operating profit of 9.36 billion yen, and net profit attributable to shareholders of 6.5 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth in sales and profits over the past five years, with a strong balance sheet and ongoing capital investment.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: TOMOKU differentiates itself through high-quality, environmentally friendly packaging solutions with strong recycling credentials, and premium housing with superior insulation and comfort. The company emphasizes reliability, innovation, and sustainability, aiming to 'gently wrap what is important to people' in both logistics and living environments.
